blocks.text: Google Docs voice typing: The browser-bound basic

Google Docs voice typing is exactly what the name suggests. It is a feature built into the Google Docs web interface. You turn it on by going to Tools > Voice typing inside a Chrome, Edge, or Safari tab. It works well if you only need to get words onto a page inside a document. It handles about 120 languages. If you are using English, you get extra commands like bolding text or changing paragraph alignment.

The main issue is the boundary. It stops working the moment you switch to another app like Mail, Slack, or Notes. You cannot use it to fill out forms on a website or write a quick message in an email client. It requires a stable internet connection because it streams your audio to Google servers. If your connection drops, your dictation stops. Google also retains your data for quality reviews and model training, which is a consideration if you handle sensitive documents.
Typeless: Built for speed and formatting

Typeless takes a different approach. It is a standalone application that runs on macOS, Windows, and mobile platforms. It is designed to be a system-wide tool. You can use it in any text field across your Mac. Its main selling point is the AI engine that removes filler words and repeats. It also formats lists and steps automatically as you speak. This saves time if you are drafting long-form content or technical documentation.

Typeless claims to be much faster than manual typing. It mentions speeds of 220 words per minute compared to 45 words per minute for a standard keyboard. Privacy is a significant focus here. The developers state that history is stored on-device and audio is not kept in the cloud. It is also ISO 27001, GDPR, and HIPAA compliant. This makes it a stronger choice for professionals who need to manage private data.
Lazur: A different take on Mac productivity

If you are looking for more than just dictation, Lazur offers a unique experience. It lives in the notch of your Mac. You do not just dictate; you interact with your screen. By holding ⌥ ⌘, you can ask Lazur about anything you see. It answers out loud. If you are stuck on a task, ask Lazur how to do it. It draws a circle around the button you need and guides you one click at a time.

Lazur handles everyday tasks like setting timers, adding events to your Calendar, or managing Apple Reminders. It can even perform web research by opening its own Chrome tabs and providing a summary. When you need to write, hold the fn key. Lazur provides clean, formatted text at your cursor in any app. It includes a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Everything stays on your Mac, and it only listens while you hold the key.

blocks.text: Choose Google Docs voice typing if you already work in Google Docs all day and want a free, zero-setup solution for simple dictation. It is fine for quick notes or short drafts where you do not mind the cloud-based processing. Do not expect it to help you outside of a browser tab.

Choose Typeless if you are a heavy writer who needs system-wide dictation. Its ability to format text and handle filler words is useful for long-form content. It is built for speed and works across multiple devices, making it a good choice for someone who needs a dedicated dictation tool.

Choose Lazur if you want a partner for your entire Mac workflow. It is more than just dictation. It helps you navigate apps, answers questions about what is on your screen, and manages your daily tasks. It is for the person who wants to get things done faster without switching between five different apps to finish one project.

faq.question: Does Google Docs voice typing work in other apps?
faq.answer: No, it is strictly limited to Google Docs and Google Slides within a web browser.

faq.question: Is Typeless free to use?
faq.answer: Typeless does not show pricing on its main site. You will need to check their pricing page directly.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur is currently designed for macOS only. Windows support is planned but not available.

faq.question: How does Lazur protect my privacy?
faq.answer: Lazur only listens and looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut keys. Audio and screenshots are not stored, and your content is never used to train AI models.

If you want a complete assistant that helps you navigate your Mac, answer questions, and handle research alongside your dictation, Lazur is the better fit.
